# PRSCheck — Full UK Landlord Licensing Reference

> The complete, machine-readable reference to UK property licensing: which councils run selective and additional (HMO) licensing schemes, the England-wide mandatory HMO rules, and the national registration regimes in Wales and Scotland. Compiled from council designations and legislation, current July 2026. Check any postcode free at https://prscheck.co.uk/check.

## The three licence types (England)
- MANDATORY HMO LICENSING: required everywhere in England for any property let to 5+ people forming 2+ households who share a kitchen, bathroom or toilet, with at least one paying rent. No storey test since 1 October 2018. Licence up to 5 years. Statute: Housing Act 2004 Part 2, SI 2018/221.
- ADDITIONAL HMO LICENSING: a discretionary council scheme extending HMO licensing to smaller HMOs (typically 3-4 sharers) below the mandatory threshold. Only applies where a council has designated it.
- SELECTIVE LICENSING: a discretionary council scheme covering ordinary private rented homes (not just HMOs) in a designated area, often street or ward level. A single-family let still needs one if the address is inside the zone. Since 23 December 2024 councils can designate schemes of any size without Secretary of State approval.

## Penalties for operating unlicensed (England, from 1 May 2026)
- Civil penalty up to £40,000 per offence (raised from £30,000 by the Renters Rights Act 2025).
- Rent Repayment Order up to 24 months rent (doubled from 12), claimable by the tenant or council, and now reaching superior (rent-to-rent) landlords.
- Unlimited fine on criminal prosecution; banning orders for serious or repeat offenders.
- Section 21 abolished 1 May 2026. Once the national PRS Database is live (rollout from late 2026), courts can refuse possession to unregistered landlords.

## Wales and Scotland
- WALES: Rent Smart Wales. All landlords must register; self-managing landlords and all agents need a licence with training. 5-year terms. Fixed penalties, unlimited fines, rent stopping orders, 12-month rent repayment orders. Mandatory HMO licensing in Wales still uses the 3-storey + 5-person + 2-household test.
- SCOTLAND: all landlords must register with each council where they let, renewing every 3 years; fines up to £50,000 for letting unregistered. HMO licence required for 3+ unrelated occupants.

## Councils with no discretionary scheme
Every other English council operates mandatory HMO licensing only (plus Wales/Scotland national regimes). Browse all 296 at https://prscheck.co.uk/councils.

## Canonical
https://prscheck.co.uk
